title: Certify v0.17.0: Part L correction and addendum, a proven bound on the truncation error of the asymptotic Newell demagnetization tensor
description: This release corrects Part L (certified Newell demagnetization-tensor tables, v0.12.0) and adds a result. Correction: through v0.16.0 the Part L note, its README entry and its certificate called a three-term asymptotic form (terms in 1/r^3, 1/r^5, 1/r^7) "OOMMF's asymptotic expansion". That form was transcribed from the demagderiv notebook (K. M. Lebecki, 2012, in the ovf2mfm repository of Boardman, Lebecki and Fangohr), which follows a 2010 pre-release of OOMMF; every demagcoef.cc on the public mirror of OOMMF releases, from 1.2a5bis to 2.1a0, carries a fourth term (1/r^9), and since 2.0a2 OOMMF chooses its switching radii from assumed error and speed models. The three-term digit counts are unchanged and correct for that truncation; Table 1 gains a four-term column, and the crossover statements now say which truncation they concern. Equation (1) of the note carried a leading minus sign copied from a cited source; with one gradient in each integration variable that sign is reversed relative to the certified values, which were always computed with the correct sign. Equation (4), the stencil, did not define its second difference; read with the standard one, it needs a leading minus sign to match its own weights. Smaller corrections are listed in CORRECTIONS.md; the metadata text of the released certificate is left byte-identical and its superseded wording is disclosed there. Addendum: for two identical axis-parallel cells with diagonal D and centre offset r > D, every tensor component and every odd truncation order n >= 3, the asymptotic series truncated at order n has error at most V D^(n-3) / (2 pi r^(n-2) (r^2 - D^2)), with a sharper shape-dependent form. The bound has the form of OOMMF's assumed error model with the cell diagonal in place of the longest edge and 1/(2 pi) in place of 1/5; its constant is attained in the limit of a thin needle, and it is loose for compact cells. The proof is in section 8 of the note; demag-scripts/check_remainder_bound.py tests both forms against every certified entry with r > D (1,162 entries of the six-cell certificate, which include the 776 of the first) in exact rational arithmetic, and series_terms.py derives the series to any order. A second certificate, demag_certificate_six_cells.json (1,310 entries), adds the thin-film cells (1, 1, 1/10) and (1, 1.3, 1/10); it passes the unchanged checker. Credit: the series and its first four terms are Donahue's (OOMMF demagcoef.cc; HMM-2007 talk). A rigorous remainder estimate with a non-explicit constant appears in Buchheit, Busse, Kessler and Rybakov (J. Comput. Phys. 559 (2026) 114885, Corollary 2.5); a dated search found no bound of the explicit form above (SWEEP-RECORD-DEMAG-BOUND-2026-11-10.md). No certified enclosure, checker logic or earlier result changed. Computations carried out with Claude (Anthropic), directed by the author.
